extracted: Notifications for 2007–2009: 822 in the CDR under the EMCDDA definition and 562 in the police registry, together 929 people. Only 455 (49%) were in both; 367 (40%) were in the CDR count only; 74 (8%) were in the police registry with a CDR cause of death outside the EMCDDA definition; 33 (4%) police-registry deaths had no CDR match (39% of them not Norwegian citizens, the rest with missing or erroneous ID numbers). Compared with deaths in both, deaths in the CDR count only were older (mean 42.7 against 35.3 years) and more often had dependence or suicide as the cause (33% against 8%); in the adjusted model morphine/codeine (odds ratio 6.89), methadone (3.69) and synthetic opioids (4.63) against heroin, no autopsy (2.66) and death in a hospital or other institution (2.61) went with being in the CDR count only. An autopsy was recorded for 715 of the 822 CDR deaths. The author states that neither police reporting nor the CDR/EMCDDA count should be considered the correct figure for drug deaths in Norway.
